title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck calls the combinatorial data of a stable curve a 'maquette'. In modern terms this is the dual graph G=(S, Â, σ): S is the set of vertices, Â the set of half-edges and σ the involution pairing them. It comes with a set I of marked points (legs) and a genus function g: S→ℕ. An MD-graph (MD for 'Mumford–Deligne' or 'modulaire') is a connected, nonempty maquette that is stable. Stable means every genus-0 vertex has total weight (valence plus number of marked points) at least 3. It also means the graph is not a single genus-1 vertex with no edges and no marked points; more generally genus-1 vertices have weight at least 1.

Proposition: an MD-graph of type (g,ν) is 'anabelian', i.e. 2g+ν≥3, equivalently 2g−2+ν>0. Here g = Σ g_α + h_1(G) and ν = |I|.

Proof on this page, case (g,ν)=(1,0). The relation 1 = Σg_α + h_1 leaves two possibilities.
(i) All vertex genera are 0 and h_1=1.
(ii) Exactly one vertex has genus 1 and h_1=0, so G is a tree. Since s_0 − s_1 = h_0 − h_1 = 1 there is one more vertex than edges.
Because ν=0, every genus-0 vertex must have valence at least 3.

In case (ii) the tree is not a single vertex, since that is the excluded unstable (1,0) maquette. So it has at least two leaves. At least one leaf has genus 0 and valence 1 < 3, a contradiction.

In case (i) all vertices have genus 0, hence valence at least 3, so there are no leaves. A connected finite graph with h_1=1 and no topological endpoints is homeomorphic to a circle. All its combinatorial vertices therefore have order 2, contradicting order ≥3.

The next page treats (g,ν) with g=0, ν≤2. There G is a tree with all genera 0. If G is a single vertex, stability gives ν≥3, contradicting ν≤2. Otherwise G has at least two leaves, each needing at least 2 marked points, so ν≥4.

Purpose: this verifies that every boundary stratum of the Deligne–Mumford compactification of M_{g,ν} lies over a hyperbolic ('anabelian') type. It prepares the definition of G-épinglage (G-rigidified) stable curves on the next page, i.e. the stratification of the boundary of M̄_{g,ν} by dual graphs, for the study of the 'structure at infinity'.
errors: No genuine error. The argument for case (i) is topological ('homeomorphic to a circle') where a one-line count would do. Connected with h_1=1 gives E=V, while all valences ≥3 gives 2E = Σ deg ≥ 3V > 2V, a contradiction.

Minor: the page asserts the dichotomy 'all g_α=0 and h_1=1, or one g_α=1 and h_1=0'. It labels 'premier cas' and 'cas 2°' only through interlinear insertions, so the numbering is confusing, but the logic is sound.
The case g=0 with a single vertex is not explicitly separated even on the next page ('ne peut être réduit à un seul sommet'). This is implicit: a single genus-0 vertex with ν≤2 is unstable.

ideas.what: Dual graph ('maquette') of a stable marked curve, with genus function on vertices; stability conditions on vertices (MD-graph)
ideas.modern_name: stable graph / dual graph of a stable n-pointed curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford (1969), Knudsen (1983); stable graphs formalized e.g. by Kontsevich–Manin, Getzler–Kapranov (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν} and the Mumford–Deligne compactification, but not this formal definition

ideas.what: Genus formula g = Σ g_α + h_1(G) and Euler characteristic s_0 − s_1 = h_0 − h_1
ideas.modern_name: arithmetic genus of a nodal curve via its dual graph

ideas.what: Every stable graph has hyperbolic ('anabelian') type 2g−2+ν>0
ideas.modern_name: nonemptiness criterion for M̄_{g,n} / stability implies 2g−2+n>0
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) uses 'anabelian' / hyperbolic type (g,ν) with 2g−2+ν>0

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine combinatorial verification that stable dual graphs have hyperbolic type. It is well known and standard. The only mildly notable features are terminological: 'maquette', 'MD-graphe', and calling the type 'anabélien' in this context.
transcription_corrections: The superscript '7' over G (written 'G^7') is not mathematical. It is likely a stray mark or a footnote/reference numeral, so read simply G=(S,Â,σ).
The insertion read as '(i.e. G contractile [?]))' belongs to the second alternative (one g_{α0}=1, h_1=0) and means G is a tree. The reading 'contractile' is plausible but uncertain.
Read '... ou bien tous les g_α sauf un g_{α0} sont nuls, et g_{α0}=1, h_1=0'. The crossed-out text after 'h_1=' in the first alternative is '1 et', so the first alternative is h_1=1.
Insertion in the last paragraph: 'un graphe 0-connexe avec h_1=1 fini sans pt. bout topologique est homéomorphe à un cercle'.
